title: NAHB/Wells Fargo Housing Market Index (November 2026) — builder confidence, 10:00 a.m. ET, and the first measurement of the sentiment-vs-data channel
source: IR: the publisher's own forward calendar — nahb.org/news-and-economics/housing-economics/indices/nahb-wells-fargo-housing-market-index-release-dates fetched direct 2026-09-06 (HTTP 200, 47,132 bytes), whose "2026 HMI Schedule" table carries the standing note "Normal release time: 10:00 AM Eastern Time" and the row "Nov. 2026 | November 17, 2026". NAHB is the producer of this series, not an aggregator, so this promotes on the same precedent as existing-home-sales-2026-11-12 (NAR's own calendar) and challenger-job-cuts-2026-09-03 (a private publisher's own release). Corroborated three ways this session, all primaries: (1) NAHB's live HMI page, /indices/housing-market-index (HTTP 200, 61,528 bytes), whose "HMI Key Findings: August 2026" block reports the August edition NAHB's own schedule dated 2026-08-17; (2) seven consecutive years of the SAME schedule page archived at web.archive.org (snapshots 20200927, 20211021, 20220928, 20230906, 20240909, 20250821, 20260105), giving 84 publisher-authored dates 2020-2026 — a forward calendar the publisher maintains, not a one-off announcement; (3) 78 of the 80 already-elapsed scheduled dates are US trading days and the schedule's mid-month Mon/Tue convention is unbroken across those seven years. Two cautions recorded rather than smoothed: the only two exceptions are 2023-06-19 and 2024-06-19, both Juneteenth market holidays, so a scheduled date is NAHB's commitment and not a guarantee the tape is open; and the live 2026 table's December row reads "December, 16, 2026" with a stray comma. The PDF twin (/-/media/NAHB/.../hmi-release-schedule.pdf) 302-redirects as of 2026-09-06 — a correction to the proposing lane, which recorded it as the 404-served-as-200 trap; the HTML page above is the working source either way. Checked 2026-09-06
notes: The residential corridor's one privately-produced release, and the ledger that answers the question it was proposed to ask. The housing-starts-2026-11-18 lane proposed this id on an explicit untested alternative: that builder SENTIMENT, not builder DATA, is the homebuilder-keyed channel the federal prints keep failing to be. This session measured it and the answer is no. Instrument: 78 NAHB-published HMI release days 2020-01-16 -> 2026-08-17 against 1,678 sessions (2020-01-02 -> 2026-09-04) of ITB/XHB/SPY daily OHLC from the Nasdaq API (Yahoo hard-429'd this runner, as it did the existing-home-sales-2026-11-12 lane; ITB 93.91 / SPY 770.19 / XHB 103.25 on 2026-09-04 reproduce the sibling ledgers exactly, and VIX 14.53 from CBOE). Because the HMI lands 10:00 — 30 minutes after the open — the pre-specified live window is the OPEN->CLOSE move and the overnight gap is a placebo. Both are null: ITB open->close 0.9559% vs 0.9627% baseline (p=0.96), XHB 0.9031% vs 0.8695% (p=0.80), ITB session range 2.2536% vs 2.0913% (p=0.21), and the placebo gap 0.5011% vs 0.5034% (p=0.97), which is the instrument confirming its own direction. The decisive test is paired: 71 of the 78 HMI days (91.0%) are the trading day immediately before New Residential Construction, and on those 71 consecutive-session pairs ITB's sentiment-day open->close is smaller than its data-day open->close 35 times out of 71 — 49.3%, a sign test at p=1.00. Sentiment and data are indistinguishable from each other and from baseline. One further finding, novel and attributed: the headline SPY overnight-gap lift on HMI days (0.4184% vs 0.3283%, p=0.065) is NOT the HMI. Splitting the 78 by whether the Fed's G.17 industrial-production release (09:15) shares the morning — 185 G.17 dates parsed from federalreserve.gov/feeds/g17.xml dc:date stamps — the 34 HMI+G.17 days read 0.4828% vs a 0.3275% clean baseline (p=0.0385) while the 44 HMI-only days read 0.3391% (p=0.85), exactly baseline; G.17 days generally read 0.4444% (p=0.0219). The pre-open belongs to the 09:15 print. That also settles the proposal's open 'a 10:00 HMI lands buried' caution as MOOT rather than true: a stacked morning changes nothing about the HMI's own window (HMI+G.17 vs HMI-only, ITB open->close 0.8503% vs 0.9894%, p=0.50), because there is no signal there to bury. 2026-11-17 is in the stacked class — retail sales and import/export prices 08:30, industrial production 09:15, MTIS 10:00. Honesty note kept on the record: 27 permutation tests were run and exactly one crossed p<0.05 (XHB open->close on New Residential Construction days, 1.1222% vs 0.8628%, p=0.047) against ~1.35 expected by chance, ITB does not corroborate it (p=0.82), and it is reported as noise rather than a finding. `symbols: []` and `impact: low` are re-derived here, not inherited. Date is `confirmed` on the publisher's own calendar; that licenses nothing, and the call is stand aside on every horizon. Discovered in the housing-starts-2026-11-18 adjacency sweep 2026-09-06; canonical file written by this event's own initial research the same day, which shadows that proposal.
